Electrical Appliances Sectional Committee, ET 32 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Electrical Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical 
Division Council. 

This standard covers the general, safety and performance requirements of mains operated clocks. 

As per the decision of the third meeting of Electrotechnical Division Council, a separate safety 
standard on clock has been brought out. In this composite standard instead of giving details of 
safety requirements, reference has been made to safety standard, IS 302-2-26 ( 1993 ) 'Safety of 
household and similar electrical appliances : Part 2 Particular requirements, Section 26 Clock'. 
It is intended to cover some more performance requirements in future on the basis of future 
developments within the country as well as at the international level. 

This standard, when published, will supersede IS 5160 : 1969 'Specification for mains-operated 
synchronous clocks', requirements of which have been covered under this standard. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the results of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised) 9 * 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard. 



IS 14145 : 1994 



Indian Standard 

MAINS OPERATED CLOCKS 
SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers general safety and 
performance requirements of mains operated 
clocks for voltages not exceeding 250 Vac 
single phase or dc. 

1.2 In addition to above, the provision of 1 of 
IS 302-2*26 ( 1993 ) shall also apply. 

2 REFERENCES

sary adjuncts to this standard:

thereunder. The details of conditions under 
which the licence for the use of Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers 
may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian 

Standards. 

9 SAFETY REQUIREMENTS 

9.1 The clocks shall comply with the require- 
ments given in 8 to 32 of IS 302-2-26 ( 1994 ). 

10 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 

10.1 The time keeping of the clocks shall be 
unaffected by a fall of voltage to 15 percent 
below the lowest rated voltage while the clock 
is in any position within 5° of the normal 
position. 

10.2 Clocks purporting to be self starting shall 
start at a voltage 15 percent below the lowest 
rated voltage in any position within 5° of the 
normal position. 

10.3 The self-starting clock shall be able to 
keep time for 24 hours with a tolerance of ± 30 
seconds while connected to the rated frequency. 

11 ENDURANCE 

11.1 For spring driven clocks with an electri- 
cally operated winding mechanism and for 
alarm system of clocks, compliance is checked 
by the test of 18.2 to 18.6 of IS 320-1 ( 1979 ). 
Other clocks are not tested for endurance. 

11.2 The clock is operated under normal load 
and at a voltage equal to 1*1 times rated voltage 
for 48 h, reduced by the running time necessary 
for the tests of 11 and 13 of IS 302-2-26 ( 1993 ). 
The clock is then operated under normal load 
and at a voltage equal to 0-9 times rated voltage 
for a period of 48 h, 

The clock is operated continuously or for a 
corresponding number of periods, each period 
being not less than 8 h. 

if the clock incorporates more than one motor, 
the operating time specifically applies to each 
motor separately. 

11.3 After the test of 11.2, the clock shall with- 
stand the electric strength test of 16.4 of 
IS 302-1 ( 1979 )♦ 



IS 14145 : 1994 



12 FINISH 

12.1 The external finish used on metal compo- 
nent shall be of non-hazardous and also of heat 
and moisture resisting nature and shall not be 
adversely affected by variation in temperature 
occurring under normal operating conditions 
or after endurance test. 

12.2 Compliance is checked by visual inspection 
after endurance test. 

13 TESTS 



13.0 Categories of Tests 



Tests are classified as type, acceptance and 
routine tests. 

13.1 Type Tests 

The tests specified in Table 1 shall constitute 
the type tests and shall be carried out on two 
samples of clocks of the same type and rating 
selected preferably at random from a regular 
production lot. Before commencement of the 
tests, the synchronous clocks shall be visually 
examined and inspected for obvious visual 
defects in respect of components, parts and 
their assembly, construction, mechanical haz- 
ards, markings, provision of suitable terminals 
for supply connections, earthing and the effecti- 
veness of screws and connections. The external 
surface finish shall be even and free from 
finishing defects. 

Table 1 Schedule of Type Tests 

( Clause 13.1 )

ii) Performance requirements 

iii) Endurance 
iv) Finish

13,1.1 Criteria of Acceptance 

Both samples shall successfully pass all the type 
tests for proving conformity with the require- 
ments of the standard. If any of the samples 



fails in any of the type tests, the testing 
authority, at its discretion, may call for fresh 
samples not exceeding twice the original num- 
ber and subject them again to all tests or to 
the test( s ) in which failure( s ) had occurred. 
No failure should be permitted in the repeat 
test( s ).
